# M03 — LSTM baseline (Phase 3)

*Generated by `python -m src.experiments.run_lstm` on 2026-09-02 02:41 UTC. Numbers trace to `results/tables/m03_lstm_*` and `results/predictions/m03_lstm_*.parquet`.*

## Scope

Roadmap Phase 3: a vanilla **LSTM** (Hochreiter & Schmidhuber 1997; Ch2 §2.5) forecasting daily realized *variance*, selected on the validation split and run through the **same** leakage-free anchored walk-forward as the Phase 2 baselines. QLIKE is primary (Patton 2011). This answers **RQ1**: does a deep sequence model beat GARCH(1,1)/EGARCH/HAR-RV on the same protocol?

## Chosen configuration

- **Features:** `['log_rv', 'oc_log_return']` (log-RV history + open-to-close return); target = log realized variance, mapped back to variance with a log-normal smearing correction.
- **Selected on validation:** hidden **128**, lookback **10**, lr **1e-03** (val QLIKE nan).
- **Network:** 1-layer LSTM, dropout 0.1, Adam, early stopping (patience 15) on a time-ordered inner-val tail.
- **Refit:** retrain every 1 fold(s); test folds every 21 days (matches Phase 2).
- **Split:** train ≤ 2015-12-31, val 2016-01-01–2018-12-31, test 2019-01-01–2022-02-25 (784 OOS days, 38 folds).

## Findings (RQ1)

The LSTM beats HAR-RV on QLIKE; the best model overall is **LSTM** (QLIKE **0.2607** vs HAR-RV **0.2745**). A formal Diebold–Mariano test (HLN-corrected, Student-t) on that pair gives stat **-0.89**, p≈**0.372** — the gap is **not statistically significant** (the Model Confidence Set over the full model board, controlling for multiple comparison, is reported in Phase 5, `m05`). The ranking is loss-function-dependent: the picture is loss-dependent — the best LSTM leads on QLIKE but HAR-RV is marginally ahead on MSE (4.18e-08 vs 4.29e-08), with MAE near-identical across the top models — a Patton-2011 reminder that the chosen metric can move the ranking.


This is the expected shape for daily equity RV: HAR-RV is a demanding benchmark on its native target (Corsi 2009; Bucci 2020; Kılıç 2025), so the value of the deep model is not assumed — it is tested. The regime-aware (Phase 5) and uncertainty-aware (Phase 6) variants build on this exact LSTM.

## Gate criteria

- [x] PyTorch `Dataset`-style sliding windows; vanilla LSTM regressor (dropout, MSE).

- [x] Hyperparameter sweep on validation (hidden × lookback × lr); heatmap saved.

- [x] Walk-forward evaluation with early stopping; leakage discipline (train-only scaling, windows end before target, HMM-style fit-on-train).

- [x] Learning curves saved.

- [x] Head-to-head vs GARCH(1,1)/EGARCH/HAR-RV on identical splits; predictions persisted.

- [x] Robustness: RV-only (HAR-matched-input) LSTM benchmarked to isolate architecture from inputs.
